text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.

- A long-standing rift between the leadership of the Christian Democratic Party (KDNP) and its parliamentary group came to a head on Tuesday as the group expelled three top party members, whereupon party president Gyorgy Giczy himself voluntarily quit his own party's parliamentary group.

- Two votes of the Parliament overshadowed all others, and had unanimous backing: the resolution on NATO membership and that call for government and public assistance for flood victims in countries north of Hungary.

- On the final day of its extraordinary summer session on Tuesday, the Parliament, in addition to its votes on NATO and flood assistance, pension reform, privatisation, the length of compusory military service and the membership of the top advisory body at the Hungarian news agency MTI. The Parliament will next meet in plenary session on September 8.
- The EU will today recommend that the EU initiate accession negotiations with Hungary and five other countries as part of an EU enlargement and restructuring strategy know as Agenda 2000.

- The European Commission ruled on Tuesday that Alitalia airlines must sell its 30 percent stake in the Hungarian airlines Malev as a condition of receiving $1.62 billion capital injection from the Italian government.
- The management of the State Privatisation Agency APV Rt will dismiss 70 to 80 employees as a result of a decision made in May on a 20 percent personnel cut this year.

- The value of the real estate portfolio to be given by Postabank to the State Privatisation Agency APV Rt in exchange for shares in various companies has dropped to 14 billion forints from the planned 17 billion forints.
- The winner of the tender for a 9.61 percent or one billion forint stake in K&H Bank will be annoiunced today by the State Privatisation Agency APV Rt. (VILAGGAZDASAG as well.)
- Four investors submitted bids for an eight billion forint stake in the steel works Diosgyori Acelmuvek Rt (NEPSZABADSAG as well.).
- Fotex's majority owner, Blackburn International has been continuously buying small stocks of shares.
